name: SPlisHSPlasH + splashsurf
role: SPH fluid simulator paired with splashsurf CLI/library for particle-to-mesh surface reconstruction
notes: 2026-11-15: Assess because the digest describes a bakeable particle simulation and mesh-sequence workflow beyond rigid-body solvers. Revisit after confirming build and Python/CLI support on target machines and cross-machine reproducibility.

2026-11-15: Assessment uncertainty: release recency and reproducible SPlisHSPlasH build/export steps on target machines were not established; assess the GPL simulator and MIT reconstruction component separately.
summary: SPlisHSPlasH simulates particle based fluids; the companion splashsurf project reconstructs SPH particle data as surface meshes, with Rust CLI/library and Python bindings. Together they support a scriptable simulation-to-mesh workflow, while simulation build and export settings remain environment dependent.
use_when: Bake particle fluid simulations and reconstruct a mesh sequence
Choose SPH particle workflows over rigid-body solvers
Use splashsurf to turn SPlisHSPlasH particle output into surface meshes
avoid_when: Use a rigid-body solver for primarily solid-object dynamics
Use Blender fluid tools when an integrated scene authoring workflow matters more

install.macos: Build SPlisHSPlasH from its official source; install splashsurf with `cargo install splashsurf` or Python bindings with `pip install pysplashsurf`
